title: Spark's Arkis investment buys guaranteed best-in-market infrastructure pricing alongside equity
content:
The Arkis terms (A.6.1.1.1.3.6.2.1.1) bundle four instruments: a SAFE "substantially mirroring the Ycombinator SAFE format"; a token warrant guaranteeing "token ownership share equal to at least 50% of Spark's share of equity ownership at the time of token launch"; a side letter carrying "most favored nation rights, pro rata rights, information rights, major investor rights, and right to elect one director"; and a commercial term — "reduced fees for use of Arkis protocol for 5 years with Spark Foundation holding the option to extend by 2 additional years, assessed as a **50% reduction vs the lowest rate of fees paid by any other user**."

The fee clause is the one that makes this strategic rather than financial. Arkis is described at A.6.1.1.1.3.6.2.1 as prime brokerage infrastructure spanning DeFi, centralized exchanges and custodians — and the immediately following section, A.6.1.1.1.3.7, commits Spark to allocating capital *through* that same infrastructure. Spark is buying into its own supplier.

Denominating the discount relative to every other user's best rate, rather than as a fixed number, is what makes it durable. A fixed fee schedule erodes as Arkis competes on price; a floating 50%-below-best guarantees Spark's cost advantage survives any future price war, and automatically improves whenever Arkis discounts for anyone else.

The token warrant at ≥50% of equity share addresses the standard failure of equity investments in protocol companies — value migrating to a token the equity holders do not own. Fixing the ratio in advance means Spark cannot be diluted by that migration.

What the Artifact does not address is the resulting related-party structure: Spark is concurrently shareholder, director-appointer, discounted customer, and the capital source flowing through the platform. Each role is documented; the conflicts between them are not.
description: The deal pairs a SAFE and token warrant with a five-year fee reduction assessed at 50% below the lowest rate paid by any other Arkis user, on infrastructure Spark then allocates capital through.
